query: 物理风险 (极端天气/海平面) 物理风险 (极端天气/海平面) 衡量企业识别、评估与管理极端天气、海平面上升等气候物理风险的能力。 重点考察：风险识别完整性、资产暴露评估深度、适应措施与业务连续性安排。 内容质量得分 • 2分：系统识别急性和慢性风险，覆盖关键资产/供应链，有量化暴露评估、适应措施及应急恢复机制。 • 1分：有风险识别与原则性措施，但缺少系统化评估或具体实施路径。 • 0分：无相关披露。 气候物理风险 急性物理风险 慢性物理风险 极端天气 暴雨 洪水 沿海洪水 台风 风暴潮 热浪 长期高温 干旱 野火 海平面上升 降水模式变化 资产暴露 气候适应 业务连续性 韧性措施 physical climate risk acute physical risk chronic physical risk extreme weather heavy precipitation flood coastal flooding typhoon storm surge heatwave chronic heat drought wildfire sea level rise changing precipitation patterns asset exposure climate adaptation business continuity resilience measures 企业识别了哪些急性物理风险（如台风、洪水、热浪）？ 是否识别海平面上升、长期高温等慢性风险？ 是否评估关键资产、运营点或供应链暴露？ 是否披露适应措施、加固改造或应急恢复安排？ 是否有量化暴露或损失评估？
instruction: Assess whether the passage provides concrete evidence for the ESG indicator '物理风险 (极端天气/海平面)'. Prefer explicit, auditable disclosure that answers: 企业识别了哪些急性物理风险（如台风、洪水、热浪）？ 是否识别海平面上升、长期高温等慢性风险？ 是否评估关键资产、运营点或供应链暴露？ 是否披露适应措施、加固改造或应急恢复安排？ 是否有量化暴露或损失评估？ Exclude or down-rank: 排除：仅有转型风险（政策、诉讼、融资）；仅有减排目标；仅有泛化气候风险管理而无物理风险内容；仅有社区防灾公益项目而无企业资产风险；区分：物理风险聚焦极端天气与海平面等物理影响及适应措施；转型风险聚焦政策法律资金变化；场景分析是评估方法，可服务物理与转型风险，但不能替代具体物理风险识别与适应披露；TCFD披露是框架完整性，不等于本指标内容充分。 Preserve relevant tables, notes, units, limitations, policies, targets, methods and coverage details.

results.text: Sustainability Report 2021 The Group is committed to identifying and controlling defective products, to ensure the products delivered meet the specified standards. The Production Department is responsible to isolate and place the defective semi-products and products in the 'Defective Products Area' first. Depending on the reasons, they are then repaired or handled by the QM Department or the Technology and Process Management Department. The repaired products shall be reassessed and confirmed by the QM Department. As for the scrapped products, the Production Department will place them in the waste area and recycle as far as possible. For major cases, they will be discussed during the quality assurance meetings, hence developing improvement measures to avoid recurrence. In order to ensure the materials' quality and supply chain stability, the Group implements sustainable supply chain management through stringent control systems and policies. The Group has also allocated different departments to undergo risk and performance assessments: Suppliers with higher scores are regarded as the major suppliers and are offered larger orders, whereas other suppliers are classified as low-priority and alternative. In order to ensure the sound performance of the major suppliers and give opportunities to the low-priority and alternative ones to improve, D&G reviews the supplier list by conducting yearly assessment on all suppliers. If the supplier fails the yearly assessment, it has to reply and provide improvement plan within two working days after the release of the assessment results. Otherwise, it will be treated as acquiesced. The supplier with improvement made would then be re-assessed. To ensure the fairness of the review mechanism, the unqualified suppliers would be classified as alternative suppliers, yet they can still undergo annual reviews. As for complaints regarding quality problems that have been found after delivery or after use, the Engineering Service Department will collect and handle them in a unified manner, and promptly report them back to the QM Department. The QM Department holds a quality meeting every two weeks, during which it formulates corresponding improvement and preventive measures based on the analysed and summarised data. Meanwhile, the Engineering Services Department shall negotiate with customers in a timely manner, including following up and reporting on the progress of the negotiations, in order to efficiently seek solutions that satisfy customers.

Sustainability Report 2021 The Group is committed to identifying and controlling defective products, to ensure the products delivered meet the specified standards. The Production Department is responsible to isolate and place the defective semi-products and products in the 'Defective Products Area' first. Depending on the reasons, they are then repaired or handled by the QM Department or the Technology and Process Management Department. The repaired products shall be reassessed and confirmed by the QM Department. As for the scrapped products, the Production Department will place them in the waste area and recycle as far as possible. For major cases, they will be discussed during the quality assurance meetings, hence developing improvement measures to avoid recurrence. In order to ensure the materials' quality and supply chain stability, the Group implements sustainable supply chain management through stringent control systems and policies. The Group has also allocated different departments to undergo risk and performance assessments: Suppliers with higher scores are regarded as the major suppliers and are offered larger orders, whereas other suppliers are classified as low-priority and alternative. In order to ensure the sound performance of the major suppliers and give opportunities to the low-priority and alternative ones to improve, D&G reviews the supplier list by conducting yearly assessment on all suppliers. If the supplier fails the yearly assessment, it has to reply and provide improvement plan within two working days after the release of the assessment results. Otherwise, it will be treated as acquiesced. The supplier with improvement made would then be re-assessed. To ensure the fairness of the review mechanism, the unqualified suppliers would be classified as alternative suppliers, yet they can still undergo annual reviews. As for complaints regarding quality problems that have been found after delivery or after use, the Engineering Service Department will collect and handle them in a unified manner, and promptly report them back to the QM Department. The QM Department holds a quality meeting every two weeks, during which it formulates corresponding improvement and preventive measures based on the analysed and summarised data. Meanwhile, the Engineering Services Department shall negotiate with customers in a timely manner, including following up and reporting on the progress of the negotiations, in order to efficiently seek solutions that satisfy customers.

In the face of the uncertainties such as the global epidemic and climate change crisis, the Group is more aware of the importance of sustainable development in combating risks, and the needs to improve the resilience of overall operations. To further promote environmental protection, the Group has integrated the concept of circular economy into its business, and is devoted to improving the environmental performance of our recycling plants. This series uses construction waste such as used and broken asphalt mixtures as raw materials for the production of recycled asphalt pavement. Compared with conventional plants, the recycling plants significantly reduce air pollution emissions and attain resource-efficient and environmentally friendly production. With the tightening of environmental requirements for operations and the global concern on environmental issues, the Group expects the market demand for such products will continue to increase.

results.text: As part of the manufacturing industry, D&G pays specific attention to production safety in the Langfang factory, where production has been identified as the main occupation risk. Therefore, the Group strives to develop a safety culture in the production sites, in which the Group arranges regular safety training for the employees, including fire drills and relevant courses, explaining the occupational hazards and safety practices in detail. To eliminate occupational hazards, the Group allocates relevant equipment and provides personal protective equipment and labour protection products for staff, such as fire extinguishing equipment, goggles and gloves.

[Content]
As part of the manufacturing industry, D&G pays specific attention to production safety in the Langfang factory, where production has been identified as the main occupation risk. Therefore, the Group strives to develop a safety culture in the production sites, in which the Group arranges regular safety training for the employees, including fire drills and relevant courses, explaining the occupational hazards and safety practices in detail. To eliminate occupational hazards, the Group allocates relevant equipment and provides personal protective equipment and labour protection products for staff, such as fire extinguishing equipment, goggles and gloves.
